hints: Resolve all four coplanar forces along orthogonal horizontal and vertical axes to find $X$ and $Y$.
Evaluate the horizontal component $X = 51.72\text{ N}$ and vertical component $Y = -24.41\text{ N}$.
Calculate the magnitude $R = \sqrt{X^2 + Y^2} = 57.2\text{ N}$ and direction $\theta = \arctan(|Y|/X) = 25.3^\circ$ below the positive x-axis.
walkthrough:
Step 1: Set up a Cartesian coordinate system.
Resolve the four coplanar forces into components along the x-axis and y-axis:
- Summing horizontal components:
$$X = \sum F_x = 51.717\text{ N}$$
- Summing vertical components:
$$Y = \sum F_y = -24.406\text{ N}$$

Step 2: Calculate the magnitude of the resultant:
$$R = \sqrt{X^2 + Y^2} = \sqrt{(51.717)^2 + (-24.406)^2} = \sqrt{2674.65 + 595.65} = \sqrt{3270.30} \approx 57.1865\text{ N} \approx 57.2\text{ N}$$

Step 3: Determine the direction of the resultant:
Since $X > 0$ and $Y < 0$, the resultant lies in the fourth quadrant:
$$\theta = \arctan\left(\frac{|Y|}{X}\right) = \arctan\left(\frac{24.406}{51.717}\right) \approx 25.26^\circ \approx 25.3^\circ$$
The resultant acts at an angle of $25.3^\circ$ below the positive x-axis (corresponding to a three-figure bearing of $90^\circ + 25.3^\circ \approx 115^\circ$).
